questions.hint: This purring pet naps in the sunniest spot of the house and says meow.
questions.fact: A cat sleeps up to 16 hours a day — napping is basically its full-time job.

questions.hint: Humans call it their best friend; it wags its tail when it is happy.
questions.fact: A dog's nose print is unique, just like a human fingerprint.

questions.hint: This pink farm animal loves rolling in cool mud puddles and says oink.
questions.fact: Pigs are very smart — they can learn tricks faster than puppies.

questions.hint: This big spotted farm animal says moo and gives us milk.
questions.fact: A cow has one stomach with four separate compartments.

questions.hint: It waddles when it walks, quacks when it talks, and paddles on the pond.
questions.fact: Ducks have waterproof feathers, so rain slides right off their backs.

questions.hint: This green hopper says ribbit and starts life as a wiggly tadpole.
questions.fact: Frogs drink water through their skin instead of their mouths.

questions.hint: It breathes underwater with gills and sparkles with shiny scales.
questions.fact: Fish were swimming in the oceans long before the dinosaurs appeared.

questions.hint: This clucking farm bird lays the eggs for your breakfast.
questions.fact: A hen can lay around 300 eggs in a single year.

questions.hint: A big wild cat with a fluffy mane, called the king of the jungle.
questions.fact: A lion's roar can be heard from 8 kilometers away.

questions.hint: This big furry forest animal loves honey and sleeps all winter long.
questions.fact: Bears can run as fast as a racehorse, even uphill.

questions.hint: This horned farm climber will munch grass almost anywhere, even on a rooftop.
questions.fact: Goats have rectangular pupils that let them see almost all the way around them.

questions.hint: A graceful forest animal; the male grows brand-new antlers every year.
questions.fact: A deer can leap almost 3 meters high — nearly the height of a basketball hoop.

questions.hint: People ride this strong, speedy animal, and it says neigh.
questions.fact: Horses can sleep standing up thanks to a special locking system in their legs.

questions.hint: This woolly farm animal says baa and gives us warm winter sweaters.
questions.fact: Sheep can recognize dozens of faces and remember them for years.

questions.hint: A legless reptile that slithers silently and tastes the air with its tongue.
questions.fact: Snakes smell with their tongues — that is why they flick them.

questions.hint: A tiny squeaky rodent with big ears and a long thin tail.
questions.fact: A mouse's tiny heart beats about 500 times every minute.

questions.hint: A giant wild cat with orange fur and bold black stripes.
questions.fact: Every tiger's stripe pattern is unique, like a human fingerprint.

questions.hint: A wild grassland animal dressed in stylish black and white stripes.
questions.fact: Scientists think a zebra's stripes help keep biting flies away.

questions.hint: A black-and-white bear that munches bamboo nearly all day long.
questions.fact: A panda can spend up to 12 hours a day munching bamboo.

questions.hint: This Australian tree-hugger clings to branches and sleeps up to 20 hours a day.
questions.fact: Koalas have fingerprints so similar to ours that they can confuse detectives.

questions.hint: A long-eared hopper that loves crunchy carrots and wiggles its nose.
questions.fact: A rabbit can rotate its ears almost all the way around to catch faint sounds.

questions.hint: A playful tree climber with a long tail who swings from branch to branch.
questions.fact: Some monkeys use sticks as tools to fish out tasty termites.

questions.hint: A slow and steady reptile that carries its own house on its back.
questions.fact: Some turtles live for more than 100 years.

questions.hint: A desert traveler with humps on its back that can go days without water.
questions.fact: A thirsty camel can drink about 100 liters of water in 10 minutes.

questions.hint: A bird in a tuxedo that cannot fly but zooms underwater like a torpedo.
questions.fact: Penguins slide on their bellies across the ice to travel quickly.

questions.hint: The tallest land animal, with a very long neck and a spotted coat.
questions.fact: A giraffe's tongue is around 50 centimeters long and dark purple.

questions.hint: A clever, playful sea mammal that chats with clicks and leaps over waves.
questions.fact: Dolphins sleep with one half of their brain awake at a time.

questions.hint: A colorful tropical bird that can copy human words.
questions.fact: A talented parrot can learn to imitate more than 100 words.

questions.hint: The largest land animal on Earth, famous for its long trunk and big ears.
questions.fact: Elephants greet each other by wrapping their trunks together, like a hug.

questions.hint: An Australian hopper that carries its baby in a cozy pouch.
questions.fact: A kangaroo can cover 9 meters in a single giant hop.

questions.hint: A pink wading bird famous for standing on one long, skinny leg.
questions.fact: Flamingos turn pink because of the tiny shrimp they eat.

questions.hint: A squishy sea creature with eight bendy arms and a very clever brain.
questions.fact: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.

questions.hint: A huge, thick-skinned mammal with a pointy horn on its nose.
questions.fact: A rhino's horn is made of keratin — the same material as your hair and nails.

questions.hint: A lizard that changes color, with eyes that look two ways at once and a curled tail.
questions.fact: A chameleon's tongue can stretch out twice the length of its body.

questions.hint: A slow, lumbering rodent covered in thousands of sharp, pointy quills.
questions.fact: A porcupine has around 30,000 quills, and they grow back if they fall out.

questions.hint: A little armored digger that wears a bony shell and can roll into a ball.
questions.fact: Some armadillos jump straight up into the air when they get startled.

questions.hint: A huge river giant with an enormous mouth and smooth, hairless skin.
questions.fact: Hippos cannot really swim — they bounce along the river bottom instead.

questions.hint: A bird that drums its strong beak against tree trunks to find tasty bugs.
questions.fact: A woodpecker can peck up to 20 times every single second.

questions.hint: The tiniest bird in the world; it hovers in mid-air and hums with fast wings.
questions.fact: A hummingbird's heart can beat more than 1,000 times per minute.

questions.hint: A great ape with very long arms and shaggy red hair that swings through rainforests.
questions.fact: Orangutans hold big leaves over their heads as umbrellas when it rains.
